title: Ari Hoenig - Wikipedia
notes: Born 13 November 1973, Philadelphia; University of North Texas alumnus (One O'Clock Lab Band); faculty at New York University and The New School. With bassist Johannes Weidenmueller, Intro to Polyrhythms Vol 1 and Metric Modulations, Expanding and Contracting Time within Form Vol 2 (Mel Bay 2009, 2012); Systems Book 1, Drumming Technique and Melodic Jazz Independence (Alfred, 2011); the DVD Melodic Drumming (2011); Rhythm Training (2014). BMW Welt jazz award 2013. Leader discography from Time Travels (1999) to Tea for Three (2024); sideman with Jean-Michel Pilc (Welcome Home, Cardinal Points, New Dreams, Threedom), Kenny Werner, Richard Bona, Tigran Hamasyan and others. Labels and some years differ from the albums' own pages: Inversations is listed as 2006, Lines of Oppression as Naïve 2012.

title: Ari Hoenig - Drummerworld
notes: Parents a conductor and classical singer and a violinist and pianist; violin and piano from six, drums from twelve; Philadelphia clubs (Ortlieb's Jazz Haus) at fourteen; three years at the University of North Texas, where he studied with Ed Soph and played in the One O'Clock Lab Band; William Paterson College from 1995; Shirley Scott. Jean-Michel Pilc Trio, Kenny Werner Trio, Chris Potter Underground, Kurt Rosenwinkel Group, Joshua Redman Elastic Band, Jazz Mandolin Project. The Ari Hoenig Quartet from 2002 (Monday nights at Fat Cat): The Painter (2004) and the DVD Kinetic Hues (2005). The Hoenig Pilc Project from 2006. Solo kit concerts on 'a regular four piece drum kit and no percussion'. Writes a regular educational column for Modern Drummer.

title: Metric Modulations: Contracting and Expanding Time Within Form, Vol. 2 by Ari Hoenig and Johannes Weidenmueller (Modern Drummer review, Michael Dawson, 5 October 2012)
notes: 'If you're familiar with the adventurous music that NYC drummer Ari Hoenig makes with his band as well as with the modernistic pianists Kenny Werner and Jean-Michel Pilc, then you know that Hoenig's a wizard when it comes to bending barlines and implying alternate time signatures without ever losing track of the form. While it may sound as if Ari is stepping out of time at random points in a tune, there's actually a very specific method to his madness.' The first book, Intro to Polyrhythms, 'dealt with the basics of implied time, which involves internalizing "core rhythms" based on various triplet groupings, quarter-note triplets, and dotted-quarter notes.' Vol. 2 'digs into advanced approaches to metric modulation, including implied time in odd-time signatures, five- and seven-note groupings in 8th notes and triplets, and five-over-four polyrhythms.' The DVD is the focus. Mel Bay, advanced, $19.99.

title: Intro to Polyrhythms, Volume 1, Ari Hoenig and Johannes Weidenmueller (Mel Bay MB21108; contents as listed by Guitar Solo Publications)
notes: Contents: Introduction; Explanation of Terms; Practice Tips; Eighth-Note Triplets; Eighth Notes; Quarter-Note Triplets in 4/4; Dotted Quarter Notes in 3/4; Dotted Quarter Notes in 4/4; Core Grooves; Displacing the Harmonic Rhythm; Chord Progressions; Suggested Listening; About the Authors. A method for 'advanced rhythm, polyrhythm, and metric / harmonic superimposition'; book and online video.

title: Ari Hoenig on Bandcamp: Book - Intro to Polyrhythms; Book - Metric Modulations Vol 2
notes: His own shop's descriptions. Intro to Polyrhythms: 'one of the best methods for learning advanced rhythm, polyrhythm, and metric/harmonic superimposition'. Metric Modulations Vol 2: the follow-up; 'The included DVD demonstrates of all the material from the book, including improvised examples by Ari Hoenig and Johannes Weidenmueller in duo as well as trio with Aaron Goldberg. Transcriptions on how to harmonically navigate through polyrhythm inside standard jazz forms are included.' Intro to Polyrhythms page: https://arihoenig.bandcamp.com/merch/book-intro-to-polyrhythms.

title: Ari Hoenig: books and video lessons (arihoenig.com)
notes: Systems Book 1: four-way coordination and 'creative melodic independence', 'jazz comping while using melodies that stress the 2nd triplet note', 'triplet displacements'. Intro to Polyrhythms: make core rhythms into core grooves and use beat displacement. Video lessons on triplet subdivisions, melodic independence, polyrhythms, metric modulation, displacements, groupings and micro timing; Melodic Drumming: 'playing melodies on the drums' and soloing melodically over a song form. The Ari Hoenig Song Book lists Lines of Oppression, Arrows and Loops, The Painter, Bert's Playground, Green Spleen, Seraphic and others.

title: Ari Hoenig Set to Release "Bert's Playground" in September (All About Jazz publicity, 19 August 2008)
notes: Read from the Wayback Machine copy. Dreyfus, his second for the label. Punk Bop: 'rooted in the bebop tradition but is also a highly communicative unit capable of changing directions at any time'. 'Hoenig gets right to business with a bright 7/8 rendition of John Coltrane's "Moment's Notice," though the intro and bass solo are set in moderate 4/4 swing.' On 'The Way You Look Tonight' 'the famous sing-songy four-bar tag becomes fodder for rhythmic displacement'. Wayne Shorter's 'Fall' 'in 5/4'. An unaccompanied 'Round Midnight, 'accessing the melody's complex contour by manipulating his drum heads'; the same techniques on 'Anthropology' and 'WB Blues' from Inversations. 'Following in the footsteps of Max Roach'.

title: Ari Hoenig: Bert's Playground (All About Jazz review, Elliott Simon, 14 March 2009)
notes: Read from the Wayback Machine copy. Personnel by track: Ari Hoenig drums; Chris Potter tenor (1, 4, 9); Will Vinson alto (3, 7); Jonathan Kreisberg guitar (1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9); Gilad Hekselman guitar (2, 10); Matt Penman bass (1, 3, 4, 7, 9); Orlando LeFleming bass (2, 6, 8, 10). Dreyfus. Hoenig's 'understated style ... a wonderfully exquisite touch'.

title: Ari Hoenig: Inversations (All About Jazz review, J Hunter, 5 March 2007)
notes: Read from the Wayback Machine copy. Ari Hoenig drums, vocals; Jean-Michel Pilc piano; Johannes Weidenmueller bass; Will Vinson alto (3); Jacques Schwarz-Bart tenor (7). Dreyfus. 'in tight, guitar-like unison with Pilc on the opening to "Anthropology"'; his tom-tom chorus on 'WB Blues' 'sounds like a subtle, spare piano line'; on 'This Little Light of Mine' he comps on the bass drum while playing the melody on the toms; the 'multi-time signature "New Found Innocence"'.

title: Ari Hoenig: Inversations (PopMatters review, Robert R. Calder, 2007)
notes: Dreyfus, released 30 January 2007. The theme of 'Anthropology' delivered 'on tuned drums'.

title: Ari Hoenig: Lines of Oppression (All About Jazz review, John Kelman, 5 August 2011)
notes: Read from the Wayback Machine copy. Live with Pilc and Francois Moutin (Ottawa 2011) he 'pushed his elbow down on his snare hard, turning it from a percussion instrument into one actually capable of melody'; on 'Moanin'' he is the lead instrument, then settles into 'a loose swing groove'. The title track 'quirkily polyrhythmic'; 'Rhythm' is his a cappella solo with vocalisations. Personnel: Hoenig drums, vocals; Tigran Hamasyan piano, vocals, beat box; Gilad Hekselman guitar, vocals; Orlando Le Fleming bass (1, 3, 5-8); Chris Tordini bass (2, 9, 10).

title: Ari Hoenig: Lines of Oppression (JazzTimes review, Lloyd Sachs, 25 October 2011)
notes: Read from the Wayback Machine copy. 'Rhythm', an exchange with beatboxing Tigran Hamasyan, runs straight into 'Rhythm-A-Ning', where Hamasyan and Hekselman 'skip and stretch past the classic melody over the leader's unstoppable phrases'; on 'Moanin'' he plays the melody on toms. 'Time signatures shift on the head of an eighth note.'

title: Lines of Oppression (Ari Hoenig, Bandcamp album page)
notes: Released 18 April 2011, Naive/AH-HA. Ten tracks: Lines of Oppression, Arrows and Loops, Wedding Song, Rhythm, Rhythm a ning, Moanin', Love's Feathered Nails, Ephemeral Eyes, How High the Moon, Higher to Hayastan. Arrows and Loops is in eleven, 'rooted in Bulgarian dance rhythms'; Higher to Hayastan a 'break-beat take on Armenian music'; of Moanin': 'I heard the melody so strongly and wanted to make it sing on the drums.'

title: DIY-Drummer: Ari Hoenig Stuff: Part 1 (blog, January 2015)
notes: A drummer's notes from transcribing Lines of Oppression. 'Rhythm': a 16-bar head with Hamasyan on beatbox, 'very rhythmically dense, and full of odd groupings of 16th notes/metric modulation'. 'Rhythm-a-ning': 'They phrase the bridge melody in long groups of 5, starting on the last beat before the bridge'; the last A is Gillespie's 'Wee'. The note value of the fives is not given.

title: Ari Hoenig, NY Standard (Fresh Sound New Talent FSNT-550, label page)
notes: Boplicity, Bessie's Blues, Stablemates, Someday My Prince Will Come, Pent Up House, In Walked Bud, Fee Fi Fo Fum. Ari Hoenig drums; Tivon Pennicott tenor (5-7); Gilad Hekselman guitar (1-3, 5, 6); Tigran Hamasyan piano (2); Shai Maestro piano (4, 6); Eden Ladin piano (3, 5); Orlando Le Fleming bass. Peter Karl Studios, Brooklyn, September 2015, except Bessie's Blues, 21 January 2010. Musica Jazz (Alessandro Manitto, 2018): Boplicity's 'repentini cambi di ritmo' (sudden changes of rhythm); a melodic drummer able to 'invent' time rather than keep it.

title: AllSolos: Ari Hoenig and the NY Standard solos
notes: Tempos measured per solo. Pent-Up House 238 (Ladin), 240 (Pennicott), 245 (Hoenig, four drum choruses, 'his ability to suggest pitch and tonality on the drums'). Bessie's Blues 263 (Hekselman), 271 (Hamasyan), 285 (Hoenig, five choruses). In Walked Bud 89, 91, 92 (Hoenig a half chorus). Someday My Prince Will Come, a waltz at 235 (Shai Maestro). Boplicity 116. Fee-Fi-Fo-Fum 118.

title: Ari Hoenig, Conner's Days (Fresh Sound New Talent FSNT-577, label page, with press reviews)
notes: Ari Hoenig drums; Nitai Hershkovits piano; Or Bareket bass. Big Orange Sheep Studios, Brooklyn, 22 November 2017. Twelve tracks including All the Things You Are, Figuration (in 11), All of You, Guernsey St. Gooseneck. Reprints Brian Charette's review (The New York City Jazz Record) and François Van de Linde's (Jazz Journal), sourced separately.

title: Conner's Days review (Brian Charette, The New York City Jazz Record, 1 September 2019; as reprinted by Fresh Sound)
notes: 'Drummer Ari Hoenig is a master of metric modulation, superimposing displaced rhythmic patterns and time signatures over preexisting ones. His books are the definitive texts on the subject.' 'All The Things You Are' 'gets an interesting 5/4 treatment, Hoenig dropping clipped drum and bass fills'. 'Cole Porter's "All of You" puts 5 over 4 and swings hard in both.' 'Guernsey St. Gooseneck' 'is more hip-hop with snappy cross stick and stuttering hi-hat'; his solo over 'the tricky ostinato'. Figuration has a 'descending bassline in 11'. 'The drum solo out is displaced funky R&B'. Whether '5 over 4' means a 5/4 laid over the 4/4 or quintuplets is not said; 'swings hard in both' reads as two meters.

title: Conner's Days review (François Van de Linde, Jazz Journal, 18 August 2019; as reprinted by Fresh Sound)
notes: 'Shifting tempo, broken time, intricate polyrhythm, the intuitive melodic artistry of Max Roach'; 'A repetitive krautrock beat divides sections of the uplifting Guernsey St Gooseneck'; All The Things You Are, 'boosted by a slyly suggested backbeat, furthermore swings with crisp, relentless drive'; brushes on Prelude to a Kiss.

title: Check Out Ari Hoenig's Musical Magic Tricks (WBGO, 2017)
notes: His 'deft use of polyrhythms, metric modulations, and displacements'; he can 'manipulate rhythm; momentarily make time signatures disappear; and superimpose new drum patterns on a set beat'. The Pauper and the Magician; Mondays at Smalls.

title: He's Got Rhythm of Every Variety (The New York Times, Ben Ratliff; as reprinted by All About Jazz news)
notes: Read from the Wayback Machine copy; the date is not on the reprint (the trio with Gilad Hekselman and Orlando Le Fleming at Smalls, about 2009). 'at regular intervals he changes the rhythm, pouring it out or stoppering it, turning its emphasis around, subdividing or refocusing it and making it follow the melody.' In Walked Bud, 'thoroughly altered: it starts and ends slowly', with 'a stretch of flat-out double time in the middle'. A live set, not a record.

title: The Solo Recordings of Ari Hoenig (All About Jazz, David A. Orthmann, 11 November 2004)
notes: Read from the Wayback Machine copy. Time Travels (1K Recordings) and The Life of a Day (Ah Ha): 'a system of replicating the exact pitches of melodies' on 'a conventional four-piece drum kit and a few cymbals'; I Mean You on snare (snares off) and both toms, the hi-hat on 2 and 4; Confirmation, 'Rarely more than a few bars pass without the drums at least alluding to something he's played on the head'.

title: Interview with Ari Hoenig (This is Jazz, Quentin Walston, 6 March 2025)
notes: On melodic drumming: first the contour of a melody on the drums, then its actual notes; the drums tuned across about an octave and more. What he practised most was playing songs.

title: Big Fat Five: Ari Hoenig shares his most influential records (The Drum Click, 11 June 2025)
notes: His five: Keith Jarrett, Belonging (Jon Christensen); The Jo Jones Trio (Jo Jones); Kenny Garrett, Trilogy (Brian Blade); Miles Davis, Nefertiti (Tony Williams); Thelonious Monk, Monk's Dream (Frankie Dunlop). The page summarises the episode; his words are not quoted.
